sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Laser Micro-Machining of Bioresorbable Vascular Polymer Stents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental legal doctrine based on French and German codes, with direct effect of EU treaties)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties (e.g., BLEU-China BIT, BLEU-Hong Kong SAR BIT)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the laws of 13 February 2018 and 25 March 2020, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract from Companies Registry of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or chamber of commerce in the shareholder’s country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Compliance Certificate of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign tax authority or civil registry of the shareholder’s country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the incorporation and financing of the Luxembourg SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / General Body of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified identification and proof of address of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuer of the identification document (government authority) and a licensed notary in the UBO’s jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille Party)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and significant shareholders against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg national FIU lists, and FATF PEP definitions; enhanced due diligence and ongoing transaction monitoring are mandatory for medical-sector licensees.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal — www.lbr.lu / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the working language of RCS filings; the corporate name must use Latin script and may be in French, German, English, or Luxembourgish, with mandatory phonetic transliteration when the ultimate foreign parent uses a non-Latin alphabet. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or improperly analogous to a public authority or existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of refusal, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request through the LBR portal with an amended name; if the refusal is upheld, a written administrative appeal may be filed with the RCS registrar by registered letter within 15 days of the second refusal. Any further refusal may be appealed to the Tribunal d’arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 30 days from notification of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a regulated Class III medical device manufacturer; a physical registered office in Luxembourg with an operational lease is mandatory. Administrative support may be delegated to a registered agent only where the agent does not substitute the required local commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 70% within the first 24 months) because the entity is subject to state licensing and AML/CFT supervision; unannounced on-site inspections may be conducted by the Directorate of Health and the Luxembourg Medicines and Health Products Inspectorate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation at Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS preliminary clearance)
Notarization of the incorporation deed and articles of association (SARL statutes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif notarial) based on share capital and complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing and registration with the Registe de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
UBO registration under the Law of 13 January 2019 (RBE filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization and certified translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents (parent certificate of incorporation, good standing certificate, board resolution, UBO identity documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities (Apostille issuing authorities) and a licensed Luxembourg translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille/certification tariffs and prevailing translation market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced AML/CFT due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening of all UBOs and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark based on number of individuals and jurisdictions screened

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, formation structuring, and issuance of a legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg hourly rate for corporate and regulatory matters

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated and amended (SARL: Articles 710-1 to 710-26, reformed by the Law of 10 August 2016); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS and RESA); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg-City; electronic filing portal: e-RCS via www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation incorporating the articles of association) filed electronically with the RCS together with the publication insert in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital: EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate from a Luxembourg credit institution, or by a sworn statement of the Managers where all shares are held by the Managers. Funds are blocked until RCS registration; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report (commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription and full cash payment of the issued share capital of EUR 12,000 be and is hereby approved; (2) that the registered office address stated in the Articles of Association, situated in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, be and is hereby adopted as the statutory seat; (3) that [Name(s)] be and is/are hereby appointed Manager(s) (Gérant(s)) with all powers granted by the Articles; (4) that the opening of a corporate bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution be approved and the Manager(s) be authorized to sign the capital payment certificate; (5) that the Manager(s) be delegated to file the deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), to arrange RESA publication, and to complete all ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and non-confusion certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS name reservation desk / e-RCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed SARL denomination against the RCS corporate-name index and trademark databases; file a name-reservation application and obtain the 'certificat de non-confusion' (availability confirmation). The name must contain 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the suffix 'SARL'.
required_dossiers: Concise description of the corporate object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS identifies confusion or an earlier similar mark, file an amended name reservation with a new denomination or obtain the trademark owner's written waiver; a rectification request may be lodged with the RCS within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital account and issuance of the bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the founders (CSSF-supervised bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'company in formation' escrow/blocked account with a Luxembourg bank; deposit the EUR 12,000 cash share capital; complete AML/KYC checks of all founders and ultimate beneficial owners; obtain the bank's capital-release attestation ('attestation de libération de capital') which is required for the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Registered office commitment or draft lease
Passport/ID and proof of residential address of each founder
CSSF-compliant AML/KYC forms and UBO identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a negative AML alert, supplement the source-of-funds file or select another credit institution; the capital remains blocked until RCS registration and cannot be withdrawn.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed and statutory articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all founders appear before the notary and execute the 'acte constitutif' containing the articles of association (statuts); verify identity and legal capacity; integrate the statutory clauses covering share transfers, manager powers, registered office and dissolution. Any in-kind contribution requires a separate report of the réviseur d'entreprises (commissaire aux apports).
required_dossiers: Passport/ID and full legal names of all founders
Draft articles of association in French/German
For corporate founders: certificate of good standing, extracts and board authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial omissions are corrected by an additional notarial act (acte rectificatif) before filing; material statutory defects can be regularized within the three-month curative period with retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and statutory publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation dossier electronically via the e-RCS portal: notarial deed, bank capital certificate or sworn declaration, consent of the registered-office owner, manager appointments and specimen signatures. Upon assessment, the RCS issues the registration extract (extrait du RCS) with the Luxembourg registration number; legal personality is acquired at registration and the deed is published in RESA.
required_dossiers: Bank capital certificate or sworn manager declaration
Consent of the owner of the registered-office premises
Identity and signature specimens of the Managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises observations, correct the dossier within one month via e-filing amendment; statutory defects are regularized by shareholder resolution or supplementary notarial act with retroactive effect before the Public Prosecutor may seek judicial dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance registrations (RBE, VAT, social security)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial-owner declaration in the RBE within one month of incorporation; submit the VAT registration application to the AEDT for the industrial manufacturing activity; register as an employer with the CCSS (O7201 form for Managers and employees) and coordinate corporate income tax / municipal business tax registration with the AEDT.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and Luxembourg registration number
Passport/ID and residential proof of Managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filing gives rise to automatic fines (up to EUR 1,250) appealable before the competent court; VAT/CCSS late registrations are cured by voluntary filing with late-payment interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Release of subscribed capital and receipt of final corporate KYC pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS registration extract and final stamped articles to the bank; the EUR 12,000 capital is released to the freely available corporate account; obtain the corporate IBAN, BIC and final bank KYC file, and verify the RCS extract and RESA publication against the executed deed.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank mandate and signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Discrepancies in the RCS extract are corrected by an e-RCS rectification request; if the bank blocks release on AML grounds, remedy by submitting further documentary evidence of funding provenance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Santé – Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments, jointly with the Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'Industrie; technical assessment by an EU Notified Body under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) for Class III devices.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a medical-device manufacturer / 'opérateur économique' under MDR Article 31 (EUDAMED) and Luxembourg national establishment authorisation ('autorisation d'établissement') under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the liberal professions and commercial undertakings; environmental operating permit ('permis d'exploitation') for the classified facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified installation ('établissement classé') under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments – standard environmental operating authorization for laser micro-machining and polymer/solvent coating; full EIA under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment may be triggered if hazardous solvent storage exceeds 10 tonnes or annual solvent consumption exceeds 15 tonnes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal network compliant with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 November 2000 (pH 6–9.5; COD ≤ 1,000 mg O2/L; TSS ≤ 600 mg/L); VOC/solvent emissions subject to EU Directive 2010/75/EU (IED) limit values for surface cleaning and coating (20 mg C/Nm³ mass concentration and fugitive thresholds); hazardous drug-eluting residues and solvents transferred only through authorized waste carriers under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and rescue clearance from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) covering detection, extinguishing and escape routes; commune building permit with structural inspection; occupational safety audit by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) for laser Class 4 interlock enclosures, clean-room ventilation, chemical hygiene and occupational medical surveillance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IF); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (TVA), registration duties and indirect taxes; Administration des douanes et accises for customs/EORI and excise. Official digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (professional e-space), the ACD 'eCDF/eDeclaration' filing platform, the AEDT 'eTVA' portal, and the RCS Luxembourg repository for the national business matricule.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Pre-incorporation name reservation and notarial deed — draft the SARL articles of association before a Luxembourg notary and subscribe the share capital (minimum EUR 12,000/advance payments). STEP 2: Register the company with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) within 1 month of incorporation; the RCS automatically allocates the 11-digit national 'matricule' (e.g., B123456) which serves as the corporate tax identifier and legal entity identifier for Luxembourg. STEP 3: The ACD assigns a direct tax file number (numéro de dossier) for IRC/ICC/IF upon RCS data transfer. STEP 4: For VAT, a taxable person must file an application with the AEDT (Form 7900/e-TVA module on MyGuichet.lu); the authority issues a Luxembourg VAT ID (format LU + 8 digits) within approximately 2 weeks. A foreign entity without Luxembourg establishment that makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg must appoint a VAT tax representative and register accordingly; a foreign entity making only exports from Luxembourg through a local manufacturing branch must register as a Luxembourg taxable person. STEP 5: Open the customs EORI number (format LU + matricule) with the Administration des douanes et accises to lodge export declarations and obtain binding origin/valuation rulings for the Class III stents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; a SARL is always an opaque, entity-level taxpayer. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal unity / group taxation under Art. 164bis LIR for fully integrated Luxembourg resident groups (100% direct/indirect control, election to pool taxable income); (ii) tax-transparency election for certain partnerships (SCS, SCSp, société particulière) which SARL parent groups may use in structuring, though the SARL itself cannot elect pass-through; (iii) IP Box election under Art. 50ter LIR yielding 80% exemption of qualifying IP income (drug-device patents, bioresorbable polymer process patents); (iv) participation exemption election under Art. 166 LIR to exempt qualifying dividends and capital gains on substantial shareholdings; (v) securitization/RAIF transparency opt-ins where structurally applicable. Hybrid mismatch and reverse-hybrid rules under ATAD 1&2 (LIR Arts. 168ter et seq.) are mandatory, not elective, and MNEs must file DAC6/Mandatory Disclosure Rules reports on reportable cross-border arrangements; no elective hybrid-neutralizing mechanism is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover (VAT-exclusive) — small-business 'franchise en base' exemption threshold under Art. 57 of the amended Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979. A SARL manufacturing coronary drug-eluting stents will generally exceed EUR 30,000 and is mandatorily registered; registration is additionally compulsory without any turnover threshold for taxable persons making intra-EU acquisitions, importers, exporters, or persons supplying taxable goods/services with an obligation to charge Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) requirement exists in Luxembourg to date. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies for supplies to Luxembourg public authorities and state bodies, using the European standard EN 16931 through the national PEPPOL network. B2B e-invoicing is permitted with recipient consent in PDF, XML, Factur-X or ZUGFeRD formats, provided authenticity of origin and integrity of content are ensured via a qualified electronic signature (QES) or EDI. All Luxembourg VAT-registered businesses must file periodic e-returns (e-TVA) and e-recaps (e-CL) electronically, and customs export/import declarations are lodged electronically through the EU Customs Decision System (AES/ICS2) via the Luxembourg single window. Transaction-level digital reporting is anticipated only upon finalization of the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including Class III coronary stents) to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated at 0% VAT provided the goods are physically removed from the EU within 3 months of the supply, and the supplier holds authentic commercial and transport documentation evidencing departure. Intra-EU dispatches of stents to taxable customers holding a valid EU VAT ID in another member state are equally zero-rated when the goods move across borders and the transaction is reported in the EC sales list (e-CL) and Intrastat dispatch declaration. Directly connected services (freight, customs clearance, handling, quality control and laboratory testing on exported goods) qualify for zero-rating as ancillary international services. Substantiation requires the exporter to keep a complete chronologically numbered export file within the statutory record-keeping period (6 years) proving the goods left the EU; input VAT on production costs is credited through the normal periodic VAT return, with VAT refund arising where input VAT exceeds output VAT in a given filing period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Export System/AES – Single Administrative Document (SAD) with MRN number issued by Administration des douanes et accises)
Bill of Lading (or CMR/Transport Document / Air Waybill — whichever is applicable) evidencing physical carriage from Luxembourg/EU to the non-EU consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/wire confirmation demonstrating actual receipt of export payment within the agreed commercial terms)
Commercial Invoice issued by the SARL (aligned with Incoterms and the customs declared value)
Packing List (itemizing stents, lots, quantities, gross/net weights, and HS Chapter 9021 classification)
EU Intra-Community Supply evidence for intra-EU dispatches (customer VAT validation printout, CMR/GRS transport order, Intrastat dispatch return, and EC Sales List reference)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg customs authorities scrutinize export evidence at audit. Inadequate or missing export documentation triggers recharacterization of the zero-rated supply as a domestic taxable supply, resulting in retroactive assessment of 17% VAT on the entire invoice amount, plus statutory late-interest ('intérêts de retard') and a minimum administrative fine. Fraudulent zero-rating claims — including false customs declarations, fictitious counterparties, or simulated exports of the drug-eluting stents — constitute tax fraud ('escroquerie fiscale') punishable under the modified general tax law (AO) and the Criminal Code with fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment; corporate directors may be held personally liable. The standard VAT assessment limitation period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or willful concealment. Any refund (credit) invoked as a result of zero-rated export sales is recoverable with interest and may be denied for a subsequent period where documentary integrity fails; export declarations are also subject to post-clearance customs audits under the Union Customs Code with potential customs debt clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks under the oversight of the European Central Bank (ECB); the BCL is the designated national central bank for balance-of-payments reporting and statistics, while exchange matters are governed by EU law and ECB regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies no foreign exchange restrictions, capital controls, or approval regimes for current-account or capital-account transactions pursuant to Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Dividend, interest, royalty, and loan-repayment remittances are unrestricted; only ordinary Luxembourg corporate income tax, net wealth tax, and potential source-state withholding tax (mitigated under EU Directives or tax treaties) apply. Cross-border payments and balances exceeding €12,500 trigger BCL external-statistics reporting obligations for resident enterprises.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, repatriation deadlines, or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts in Luxembourg. Exporters may freely retain revenues in any convertible currency, maintain bank accounts abroad (subject to BCL statistical reporting when thresholds are met), and convert to euro at market rates. All settlements must nonetheless be documented for VAT, customs, and transfer-pricing compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low as a primary banking channel; Medium as a supplementary payment-collection rail. An EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) can passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and offer SEPA credit transfers, instant payments, and select SWIFT corridors, but cannot issue documentary letters of credit, provide trade finance, deliver term lending, or operate sophisticated liquidity pooling for a Class III medical device manufacturer. Intangible EMI onboarding may also amplify correspondent-bank counterparty risk in high-risk medical sectors; therefore restrict EMI usage to collection-only or small-balance escrow flows and never designate it as the sole treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For tier-1 Luxembourg banks, at least one physical interview with an authorised director and ultimate beneficial owners is effectively mandatory for a Class III medical device exporter. Remote onboarding via qualified electronic identification or video verification is legally possible under Luxembourg AML rules, but the medical-device manufacturing profile, high per-unit invoice values, and cross-border trade portfolio trigger enhanced due diligence and a domestic banking-relationship risk decision. In all realistic scenarios, directors must attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg head office or in the presence of a Luxembourg notary or designated embassy/consular officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry and special statutory license trigger (Class III medical device manufacturer).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Ministry of Health manufacturing license; EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) CE mark certificate for the drug-eluting coronary stent; ISO 13485:2016 QMS certificate; notified-body approval and inspection outcomes; latest Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) audit report; product registration and adverse-event vigilance records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex indirect shareholding or multi-tier cross-border investor structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully traced capitalization table and UBO declaration (register of beneficial owners-relevant); notarised share subscription acts and board minutes; Luxembourg RCS registration extracts; certified copies of passports/IDs of all natural-person UBOs; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; tax-residence certificates for all intermediate and parent undertakings; and a substance memorandum evidencing the Luxembourg SARL's real presence, employee payroll, and decision-making power.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, high-value cross-border wires to/from non-EEA medical distributor jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML-compliant counterparty screening lists (sanctions, PEP, adverse media); executed supply and distribution agreements; commercial invoices with Incoterms; air-waybills and customs export/import documentation; audited annual financial statements; cash-flow projections demonstrating macroeconomic consistency; and an up-to-date transfer-pricing documentation file covering all intercompany pricing policies, including operating-margin benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-account utilisation or abnormal transaction velocity inconsistent with genuine trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Confirmed BCL balance-of-payments declaration submissions; documentary evidence of physical goods movement including packing lists, bills of lading, and customs releases; independent cargo insurance certificates; bank-to-bank reference letters issued by prior relationship banks; and a written treasury policy prohibiting shell-entity use or pass-through flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital contributions are remitted via SWIFT MT103 or TARGET2 euro credit transfer from the parent/shareholder bank, using the inbound transaction purpose code for direct investment equity under the ECB BOP classification (equity capital). The Luxembourg notarial deed evidencing the capital increase, together with the updated articles of association and commercial-register office reference, must be supplied to the receiving bank. Funds are held in a dedicated capital escrow account until the notary certifies the contribution and the RCS reflects the new share capital; balances and transactions above €12,500 enter the BCL monthly statistical reporting stream.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for raw materials and production equipment are executed through SWIFT MT103 payments (or SEPA Credit Transfer in euro for EU counterparties) using the standard goods-trade purpose code. For high-value polymer purchases or precision machine tools, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP600 or eUCP) confirmed by a Luxembourg tier-1 bank is the preferred rail, minimising pre-shipment risk. Export receivables are collected via confirmed at-sight LCs or direct SWIFT MT103 client-initiated transfer, with all underlying customs, VAT, and invoice records retained for audit. Where non-EEA buyers require non-euro settlement, banks process conversion under the company's external-trade treasury limits and mark-up disclosures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (deliverable and non-deliverable) executed under an ISDA/CSA or domestic master agreement with a Luxembourg-authorised credit institution, provided a genuine underlying trade exposure is evidenced
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) with underlying receivables or payables exposure, settled in euro
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to hedge long-term intercompany loan or equipment financing exposures, subject to board-approved treasury policy and EMIR clearing obligations if thresholds apply

FX options and zero-cost collars to cover contingent trade exposures (e.g., tender or large distributor orders), permitted where the premium is funded from operating cash flow and position limits are documented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and RESA electronic collection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval must be given within six months of the financial year end. For a 31 December year end the final RCS filing deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After formal notice, late filing exposes the SARL and its managers to commercial court proceedings, daily astreinte payments, fines, civil director liability, and, in persistent default, court-ordered dissolution or strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner data in the Luxembourg UBO Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March; the confirmation certifies that the disclosed beneficial ownership information remains accurate as of that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation may incur criminal penalties under Luxembourg UBO law: imprisonment of six months to three years and/or a fine of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000; repeated default may also facilitate RCS deregistration or strike-off actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is exempt from statutory independent audit unless, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet in excess of EUR 4.4 million, net turnover in excess of EUR 8.8 million, and an average workforce of more than 50 employees. An audit is also required where the SARL belongs to a group that must prepare consolidated accounts or where applicable sectoral regulation, such as special licensing in Class III medical device manufacturing, imposes certified financial review obligations beyond Luxembourg company law thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the amended Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts and company books, consistent with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts and mandatory for issuers of securities admitted to trading on an EU regulated market.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL's manager (gérant) must review the RBE declaration every calendar year and submit an online confirmation of accuracy before 31 March. Any change in beneficial ownership, including a shareholding transfer that alters economic entitlement, must be reported to the RBE within one month of the change and simultaneously recorded in the internal register of members. The confirmation is signed electronically by an authorised person; notarisation is not required unless the underlying share transfer contains formal requirements under the articles of association.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales et des décisions des associés)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–3,500 per annum for a licensed Luxembourg corporate agent providing registered office, domiciliation, and corporate secretarial services to a SARL with a medical device manufacturing risk profile.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000–35,000 per audit for a small or medium SARL without group consolidation; USD 35,000–80,000 where Luxembourg GAAP/IFRS consolidation, intercompany pricing, or complex statutory book packages are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City statutory headline rate (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); headline corporate income tax alone is 17%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential reductions: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (min. 10% holding or EUR 1.2m cost, subject to substance); IP box exempting 80% of qualified IP income (effective aggregate rate approx. 5%); investment tax credit up to 8%-12% of eligible capital investments; arm's-length financing structures and ATAD-compliant hybrid measures may lower effective burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 780 (Modèle 780) Corporation Tax Return, filed electronically through MyGuichet / MyTax (guichet.lu) portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes (AED)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance CIT instalments are payable as required by the AED
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory baseline: the return is due by 31 May following the fiscal year-end; the AED may extend filing to 31 December where the return is filed electronically by a registered tax adviser

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARL name, RCS number, national tax number, registered office, legal form, principal activity (ISIC 3250: drug-eluting coronary stent manufacture / Class III MedTech), and director/manager particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) identification; attach foreign registration proving the non-resident status and stated Luxembourg business licence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year; confirm whether this is the first, final, or short-period return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE's accounting period; align with the foreign head-office fiscal year unless separate Luxembourg statutory accounts have been prepared

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per Luxembourg GAAP audited annual accounts before direct income taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the taxable profit attributable to the Luxembourg PE, allocated under OECD PE profit attribution and Luxembourg administrative arm's-length principles

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible charges: fines, corporate taxes, non-arm's-length interest, excessive management fees, unjustified provisions, and expenses lacking proper documentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reinstate expenses not economically connected with the PE and those for which transfer pricing documentation is absent or unreliable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct qualifying exempt dividends and capital gains under the Luxembourg participation exemption regime, where statutory holding period and substance requirements are met
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only for PE-held qualifying participations that meet the 10%/12-month or EUR 1.2m cost threshold and genuine substance conditions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior taxable losses within the five-year carry-forward limit, stating the year and amount of each loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses generated by the same Luxembourg PE may be used; losses incurred by the foreign head office cannot be transferred to the Luxembourg return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine the taxable base for communal business tax (impôt commercial communal), including apportionment for multiple communes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are liable for municipal business tax on PE profits allocated to each Luxembourg commune in which the PE operates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 7% solidarity surcharge to the assessed corporate income tax after all exemptions, deductions, and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the surcharge on the Luxembourg CIT attributable to the PE, reducing it only by applicable treaty credit allocable to PE profits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default assessment (taxation d'office), a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax, monthly late-payment interest at the statutory rate (currently 0.8%), and criminal fines or imprisonment where non-filing is wilful under the Luxembourg General Tax Law

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying 10% holdings held for at least 12 months; DTA reduced rates generally 0%-15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must submit a relief or refund request to the Luxembourg AED together with a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), proof of ownership and holding period, legal existence certificate, and anti-abuse / beneficial-ownership declarations. Where no prior authorisation is obtained, the payer withholds 15% statutory tax and the non-resident applies for refund within the applicable limitation period, generally three years. EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest & Royalties Directive relief follow the same prior-authorisation or refund route.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on outgoing royalties is 0%; ordinary arm's-length interest is also subject to 0% domestic withholding. The 15% movable-capital withholding tax applies chiefly to dividends, liquidation proceeds, and certain shareholder-debt interest. Treaty rates for royalties are generally 0%, and for interest 0%-10%, subject to beneficial ownership, substance, and DTA limitations; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive supplies 0% withholding tax for qualifying associated companies

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Luxembourg Master File / Local File is expected when aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 in a fiscal year or when the AED requires documentation under OECD-aligned rules; Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, economic substance is decisive under general anti-abuse and treaty-application rules. A SARL manufacturing or distributing coronary stents must maintain real local premises, qualified directors or managers, board decisions in Luxembourg, actual P&L risk, local bank accounts, and documentary substance. Artificial shell arrangements are disregarded under Article 6 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law and the ATAD GAAR, leading to denial of tax residence certificates, participation exemption, DTA rates, and EU withholding relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting medical-device sales revenue, recording fictitious CRO or stent manufacturing invoices, destroying accounting records, or knowingly submitting inaccurate Form 780 returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default assessment and restitution of evaded tax; administrative penalty up to 10%-100% of unpaid tax; default interest; criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg General Tax Law with fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and gérants who sign or approve false returns are personally liable for civil restitution of evaded tax; the corporate veil is pierceable to permit asset seizure, travel bans during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment for tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SARL with no staff, no premises, and no actual management as a passive intermediary for drug-eluting stent royalties, distribution commissions, or IP transfers solely to shift profit into Luxembourg or a treaty jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the artificial structure; denial of Tax Residency Certificate, participation exemption, and EU Directive benefits; recharacterization of income with additional CIT, municipal business tax, and solidarity surcharge; deemed distributions subject to 15% dividend WHT; penalties and default interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are personally liable for restitution of denied tax benefits; courts pierce the veil when the SARL is a mere façade; travel bans and imprisonment can be imposed where the shell arrangement is part of criminal tax fraud or money laundering

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying non-arm's-length pricing to coronary stent product sales, IP royalties, intercompany loans, or management fees; failure to prepare Local/Master File and TP benchmarking; incomplete or contradictory documentation for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length re-determination by the AED; reassessment of CIT, municipal business tax and solidarity surcharge; monthly default interest; administrative penalty of up to 10% of adjusted tax; criminal sanctions where intentionally false transfer pricing documentation is filed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false TP documentation or fail to maintain required accounting records are jointly and severally liable for additional tax, penalties, and interest; personal exposure includes civil restitution, disqualification, travel restraint, and imprisonment for fraudulent evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and AML / Money-Laundering Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividends as loans, management fees, or tax-free capital reductions to avoid the 15% Luxembourg dividend WHT; receiving unexplained commissions or LC/SWIFT proceeds from high-risk shell distributors for Class III stents; failure in AML KYC, beneficial ownership, and PEP checks
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as a dividend and imposition of 15% WHT, late-payment penalties, and default interest; Luxembourg AML sanctions include fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; foreign anti-bribery and medical-device fraud penalties may also be extended
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unlawfully withheld taxes and for distributions made without sufficient distributable reserves; AML compliance officers and managing directors face criminal liability, travel bans, freezing and confiscation of assets, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced for deliberate AML breaches
